over 80% of the sequenced human NotI sites are linked to CpG rich islands.
the NotI sites are highly associated with CpG islands and that the CpG rich regions are often found around the NotI sites in the sequenced DNA.

84% of NotI fragments in human DNA are associated with CpGs, which is consistent with the prediction that NotI sites in human genome are present in CpG islands at a frequency of 89% and that 63 new CpG islands were identified in this study.

the NotI sites in the human genome are highly likely to be associated with CpG islands, and that this association is very useful for the isolation and characterization of the associated genes.

the NotI linking DNA clones are useful for ordering of NotI fragments as well as for identification of genes associated with CpG islands.

the NotI sites are often associated with CpG islands and therefore cloning of NotI fragments can be a powerful strategy for isolation of CpG islands and genes related to them.
